```{r}
#| label: fig-data-exploration-all
#| warning: false

#| fig-height: 12
#| fig-cap: "1-Week Time Course of All System Variables"

# Load core packages
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(here)
library(janitor)

# 1. Read and clean the data
hvac_data <- read_csv(here("../HVAC/data/Turin/HVAC_NE_EC_19-21.csv")) %>%
  clean_names()

# 2. Clean the timestamp and extract a subset
hvac_clean <- hvac_data %>%
  mutate(
    timestamp = ymd_hms(timestamp) 
  )

# Extract the first week of November
hvac_week <- hvac_clean %>%
  filter(
    timestamp >= ymd("2019-11-01", tz = "UTC"), 
    timestamp < ymd("2019-11-08", tz = "UTC")
  )

# 3. Plot all 10 variables
hvac_plot_all <- hvac_week %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -timestamp, 
    names_to = "Variable", 
    values_to = "Value"
  )

ggplot(hvac_plot_all, aes(x = timestamp, y = Value, color = Variable)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~Variable, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Comprehensive 1-Week HVAC Telemetry",
    subtitle = "Turin Dataset: Nov 1 - Nov 7, 2019",
    x = "Time", 
    y = "Measurement"
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

- `power`: The power required by the fans [kW]. This is the instantaneous electrical demand. It shows a "block" pattern, representing the fan motors turning on, running at a steady state, and shutting off.
- `energy`: The energy required by the fans [kWh]. Power is the instantaneous rate, energy is the accumulated electricity consumed. The jagged, sawtooth pattern on top of the blocks is characteristic of accumulation over a 15-minute intervals.
- `rh_outdoor` (Outdoor Relative Humidity): The relative humidity of the outside air [%]. It dips during the warmest part of the day and peaks at night when the air cools.
- `rh_return` (Return Relative Humidity): The relative humidity of the return air [%]. Heating a volume of air lowers its relative humidity:  every time the system turns on to heat the space (`power`, `energy`), this indoor humidity drops.
- `rh_supply` (Supply Relative Humidity): The relative humidity of the supply air [%]. It tends to mirrors the return humidity but is physically altered by the heating coils.
- `sp_return (Setpoint Return)`: Tthe temperature setpoint of the return air [°C]. It represents the target temperature for the rooms.
- `t_outdoor (Outdoor Temperature)`: The ambient temperature outside [°C]. Natural diurnal (day/night) weather cycles.
- `t_return` (Return Temperature): The temperature of the air pulled back from the rooms into the HVAC unit [°C]: proxy for the actual room temperature.
- `t_saturation` (Saturation Temperature): The saturation temperature in the humidifier [°C]. Relates to the dew point the system maintains to prevent the air from becoming too dry when heated.
- `t_supply` (Supply Temperature): The temperature of the conditioned air being pushed into the rooms [°C]. To change the room temperature (t_return) to the target (sp_return), the system has to blast much warmer/colder air.

```{r}
#| label: fig-pairs-plot
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 12
#| fig-cap: "Scatterplot matrix with correlation-mapped backgrounds (Sampled at n=5000)"

library(GGally)

# 1. Custom function to calculate correlation and map it to a background color
custom_scatter_bg <- function(data, mapping, ...) {
  x_data <- eval_data_col(data, mapping$x)
  y_data <- eval_data_col(data, mapping$y)
  
  corr <- cor(x_data, y_data, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  
  color_fun <- colorRamp(c("#f8766d", "white", "#00bfc4")) 
  scaled_corr <- (corr + 1) / 2 
  
  rgb_vec <- color_fun(scaled_corr)
  hex_color <- rgb(rgb_vec[1], rgb_vec[2], rgb_vec[3], maxColorValue = 255)
  
  ggplot(data, mapping) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, 
             fill = hex_color, alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_point(...)
}

# 2. Generate the plot
p_pairs <- hvac_clean %>%
  select(-timestamp) %>% 
  sample_n(5000) %>% 
  ggpairs(
    lower = list(continuous = wrap(custom_scatter_bg, alpha = 0.1, size = 0.5)),
    upper = list(continuous = wrap(custom_scatter_bg, alpha = 0.1, size = 0.5)),
    title = "Pairwise Scatterplot Matrix (HVAC Telemetry)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "gray80", fill = NA)
  )

p_pairs
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-network-graph

# install.packages(c("igraph", "ggraph")) # Run in console if needed
library(igraph)
library(ggraph)
library(dplyr)

# 1. Calculate the baseline correlation matrix (excluding timestamp)
cor_matrix <- cor(hvac_clean %>% select(-timestamp), use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

# 2. Threshold the matrix to create an unweighted adjacency matrix
#    Lowered to 0.8 to capture the primary temperature and humidity groupings
adj_matrix <- ifelse(abs(cor_matrix) > 0.8, 1, 0)

# 3. Remove self-loops (a variable is always perfectly correlated with itself)
diag(adj_matrix) <- 0

# 4. Convert the matrix into an undirected igraph object
g <- graph_from_adjacency_matrix(adj_matrix, mode = "undirected")

# 5. Plot the network graph
set.seed(42) # Ensures consistent spatial layout
ggraph(g, layout = "fr") + 
  geom_edge_link(color = "gray70", width = 1.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_node_point(size = 14, color = "lightblue") +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name), color = "black", size = 3.5, fontface = "bold") +
  theme_void() +
  labs(
    title = "HVAC Feature Dependency Network",
    subtitle = "Connected components defined by absolute correlation > 0.8"
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-components-threshold
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "Network fragmentation across correlation thresholds"

library(igraph)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)

# 1. Calculate the baseline correlation matrix (excluding timestamp)
cor_matrix <- cor(hvac_clean %>% select(-timestamp), use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

# 2. Define a sequence of thresholds from 0 to 0.99
thresholds <- seq(0, 0.99, by = 0.01)

# 3. Function to calculate number of components for a given threshold
count_components <- function(th) {
  # Create adjacency matrix for the current threshold
  adj_matrix <- ifelse(abs(cor_matrix) > th, 1, 0)
  diag(adj_matrix) <- 0
  
  # Build graph and count components
  g <- graph_from_adjacency_matrix(adj_matrix, mode = "undirected")
  components(g)$no
}

# 4. Map the function across all thresholds
component_counts <- map_dbl(thresholds, count_components)

# 5. Create a dataframe for plotting
df_thresh <- data.frame(
  Threshold = thresholds,
  Components = component_counts
)

# 6. Plot the relationship as a step-like function
ggplot(df_thresh, aes(x = Threshold, y = Components)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "navy", size = 1.5, alpha = 0.4) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(1, 10, by = 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Network Fragmentation Profile",
    subtitle = "Tracking how the feature graph breaks into isolated components",
    x = "Absolute Correlation Threshold (|r|)",
    y = "Number of Connected Components"
  ) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-spectral-analysis
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 15
#| fig-cap: "Power Spectral Density (Frequency Domain)"

library(purrr)

# 1. Custom function to calculate the periodogram
get_periodogram <- function(series_name, data) {
  
  # Extract and mean-center the signal to remove the DC offset (0 frequency)
  x <- na.omit(data[[series_name]])
  x <- x - mean(x)
  
  n <- length(x)
  
  # Compute Fast Fourier Transform
  p <- Mod(fft(x))^2 / n
  
  # We only need the first half of the spectrum (Nyquist limit)
  half_n <- floor(n / 2)
  p <- p[2:(half_n + 1)] 
  
  # Frequencies: convert from cycles-per-observation to Cycles per Day (cpd)
  # 15 min intervals = 96 observations per day
  freq <- (1:half_n) / n * 96 
  
  tibble(
    Variable = series_name,
    Frequency_cpd = freq,
    Power = p
  )
}

# 2. Select key distinct variables representing weather, load, and effort
vars_to_analyze <- c("energy", "power", "rh_outdoor", "rh_return", "rh_supply",
                     "sp_return", "t_outdoor", "t_return", "t_saturation", "t_supply")
spectra_data <- map_dfr(vars_to_analyze, ~get_periodogram(.x, hvac_clean))

# 3. Plot the periodograms
ggplot(spectra_data, aes(x = Frequency_cpd, y = Power, color = Variable)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(~Variable, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  # Focus strictly on low-frequency macro cycles (0 to 4 cycles per day)
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 2)) + 
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = 0:4, 
    labels = c("0", "1/day (24h)", "2/day (12h)", "3/day (8h)", "4/day (6h)")
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Spectral Decomposition of HVAC Telemetry",
    subtitle = "Identifying dominant cyclical periods via Fast Fourier Transform",
    x = "Frequency",
    y = "Spectral Power"
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10)
  )
```

`power`: drop

`time_stamp`

`is_weekend` (from time_stamp)

`energy` (Raw State)

`energy_lag_24h` (Schedule context)

`energy_deriv_15m` (State transition context)

`rh_outdoor` (Raw context)

`rh_outdoor_lag_24h` (Weather shifts)

`delta_rh` =  `rh_return` - `rh_supply` (The active moisture control work)

`delta_rh_deriv_15m` (Sudden state changes in moisture control)

`t_outdoor` (Raw weather)

`t_outdoor_lag_24h` (Weather shift)

`t_saturation` (Raw state)

`t_saturation_deriv_15m` (Sudden humidifier faults)

`delta_t` = `t_return` - `t_supply` (The active heating work): 

`delta_t_deriv_15m` (Sudden loss or surge of heating power)

`temp_error` (How far off target the building is) $t\_return - sp\_return$

`sp_return`

```{r}
#| label: feature-engineering-pipeline
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: true

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(lubridate)
library(slider) 

hvac_features <- hvac_clean %>%
  # 0. Catch any stray NAs in the timestamp column before sequencing
  filter(!is.na(timestamp)) %>%
  # 1. Ensure the data is perfectly continuous in 15-minute increments
  complete(
    timestamp = seq(
      min(timestamp, na.rm = TRUE), 
      max(timestamp, na.rm = TRUE), 
      by = "15 mins"
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(timestamp) %>%
  mutate(
    # 2. Context & Control
    is_weekend = if_else(wday(timestamp, week_start = 1) %in% c(6, 7), 1, 0),
    temp_error = t_return - sp_return,
    
    # 3. Common-Mode Rejection (Physics)
    delta_t = t_return - t_supply,
    delta_rh = rh_return - rh_supply
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # 4. Cyclical Lags
    t_outdoor_lag_24h = t_outdoor - lag(t_outdoor, n = 96),
    rh_outdoor_lag_24h = rh_outdoor - lag(rh_outdoor, n = 96),
    energy_lag_24h = energy - lag(energy, n = 96),
    
    # 5. Instantaneous Derivatives
    energy_deriv_15m = energy - lag(energy, n = 1),
    delta_t_deriv_15m = delta_t - lag(delta_t, n = 1),
    delta_rh_deriv_15m = delta_rh - lag(delta_rh, n = 1),
    t_return_deriv_15m = t_return - lag(t_return, n = 1),
    t_saturation_deriv_15m = t_saturation - lag(t_saturation, n = 1),
    
    # 6. Volatility 
    t_supply_roll_sd_1h = slider::slide_dbl(t_supply, sd, .before = 3, .complete = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  # 7. Purge all artifacts (including the summer gap NAs)
  drop_na()

glimpse(hvac_features)
```


```{r}
#| label: fit-isolation-forest
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "Isolation Forest Anomaly Scores over Time"

library(isotree)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# 1. Isolate the feature matrix (dropping the timestamp)
train_data <- hvac_features %>%
  select(-timestamp)

# 2. Fit the Isolation Forest
# ntrees = 500 ensures variance stabilization
# sample_size = 256 prevents anomaly masking
set.seed(42) 
iso_model <- isolation.forest(
  train_data,
  ntrees = 500,
  sample_size = 256,
  missing_action = "fail" # Our drop_na() ensures a clean matrix
)

# 3. Score the dataset
# predict() drops the data down the fitted forest and returns the bounded score [0, 1]
hvac_scored <- hvac_features %>%
  mutate(anomaly_score = predict(iso_model, train_data))

# 4. Visualize the temporal anomaly profile
ggplot(hvac_scored, aes(x = timestamp, y = anomaly_score)) +
  geom_line(color = "slategray", alpha = 0.8) +
  # Visual threshold for investigation (scores > 0.6 are generally considered anomalous)
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.6, linetype = "dashed", color = "darkred", linewidth = 1) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "HVAC System Dynamic Anomaly Profile",
    subtitle = "Scores approaching 1.0 indicate severe structural breaks in mechanical behavior",
    x = "Time",
    y = "Anomaly Score (s)"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: qc-seed-stability
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: true
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: "Stability Check: Anomaly Scores across Random Seeds"

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# 1. Fit Model A 
iso_model_A <- isolation.forest(
  train_data,
  ntrees = 500,
  sample_size = 256,
  missing_action = "fail",
  seed = 42
)

# 2. Fit Model B 
iso_model_B <- isolation.forest(
  train_data,
  ntrees = 500,
  sample_size = 256,
  missing_action = "fail",
  seed = 123
)

# 3. Score and Combine
qc_data <- tibble(
  score_A = predict(iso_model_A, train_data),
  score_B = predict(iso_model_B, train_data)
)

# 4. Calculate Convergence Metric
stability_cor <- cor(qc_data$score_A, qc_data$score_B)

# 5. Visualize the Variance
ggplot(qc_data, aes(x = score_A, y = score_B)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 0.5, color = "darkblue") +
  # Reference line for perfect agreement
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, color = "darkred", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Isolation Forest Convergence Check",
    subtitle = sprintf("Pearson Correlation (Seed 42 vs Seed 123): %.4f", stability_cor),
    x = "Anomaly Score (Seed 42)",
    y = "Anomaly Score (Seed 123)"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: calculate-p-values
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: false

# 1. Fit the empirical distribution to the scores
score_ecdf <- ecdf(hvac_scored$anomaly_score)

# 2. Calculate percentiles and p-values
hvac_scored <- hvac_scored %>%
  mutate(
    percentile = score_ecdf(anomaly_score),
    # p-value: the probability of seeing a score this high or higher
    p_value = 1 - percentile 
  )

# 3. View the top anomalies with their new statistical context
top_anomalies_stat <- hvac_scored %>%
  filter(anomaly_score > 0.6) %>%
  arrange(desc(anomaly_score)) %>%
  select(
    timestamp, anomaly_score, p_value,
    is_weekend, sp_return, temp_error, delta_t
  )

# Display the top 5
head(top_anomalies_stat, 5)
```

```{r}
#| label: beta-mle-fit
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: true
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "Empirical Density vs MLE Beta Distribution"

library(MASS)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Calculate Method of Moments (MoM) to use as starting values for MLE
scores <- hvac_scored$anomaly_score
mu <- mean(scores)
var_x <- var(scores)

alpha_mom <- mu * ((mu * (1 - mu) / var_x) - 1)
beta_mom <- (1 - mu) * ((mu * (1 - mu) / var_x) - 1)

# 2. Fit the Beta distribution using Maximum Likelihood Estimation
beta_mle <- fitdistr(
  scores, 
  densfun = "beta", 
  start = list(shape1 = alpha_mom, shape2 = beta_mom)
)

alpha_est <- beta_mle$estimate["shape1"]
beta_est <- beta_mle$estimate["shape2"]

cat(sprintf("MLE Estimates:\nAlpha: %.4f\nBeta: %.4f\n\n", alpha_est, beta_est))

# 3. Superimpose the theoretical Beta curve on the empirical data
ggplot(hvac_scored, aes(x = anomaly_score)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 100, fill = "slategray", alpha = 0.5) +
  # Empirical Density (Dark Blue)
  geom_density(color = "darkblue", linewidth = 1) +
  # Theoretical Beta Density (Bright Red Dashed)
  stat_function(
    fun = dbeta, 
    args = list(shape1 = alpha_est, shape2 = beta_est), 
    color = "red", 
    linetype = "dashed", 
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.6, linetype = "dashed", color = "darkred", linewidth = 1) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Model Fit: Empirical Density vs MLE Beta Distribution",
    subtitle = "Red Dashed = Theoretical Beta Fit | Dark Blue = Empirical Data",
    x = "Anomaly Score (s)",
    y = "Density"
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: fault-signature-clustering
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: false

# 1. Isolate the severe structural breaks
severe_anomalies <- hvac_scored %>%
  filter(anomaly_score > 0.6)

# 2. Select ONLY the physical/engineered features for clustering
# Explicitly using dplyr::select to prevent MASS collision
cluster_data <- severe_anomalies %>%
  dplyr::select(
    temp_error, delta_t, delta_rh,
    energy_deriv_15m, delta_t_deriv_15m,
    t_supply_roll_sd_1h
  )

# 3. Scale the data (Critical: Energy in kWh must not dominate Temp in Celsius)
cluster_scaled <- scale(cluster_data)

# 4. Compute Euclidean distance and build the hierarchical tree
dist_matrix <- dist(cluster_scaled, method = "euclidean")
hc_model <- hclust(dist_matrix, method = "ward.D2")

# 5. Cut the tree into 3 distinct fault signatures
severe_anomalies <- severe_anomalies %>%
  mutate(fault_signature = as.factor(cutree(hc_model, k = 3)))

# 6. Summarize the mechanical profile of each fault signature
fault_profiles <- severe_anomalies %>%
  group_by(fault_signature) %>%
  summarize(
    event_count = n(),
    avg_temp_error = mean(temp_error, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_delta_t = mean(delta_t, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_energy_surge = mean(energy_deriv_15m, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_volatility = mean(t_supply_roll_sd_1h, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Display the diagnostic profiles
print(fault_profiles)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)

# 1. Sort and calculate temporal gaps within each physical cluster
temporal_events <- expanded_anomalies %>%
  arrange(cluster, timestamp) %>%
  group_by(cluster) %>%
  mutate(
    # Calculate time since previous anomaly in the SAME cluster
    time_gap = as.numeric(difftime(timestamp, lag(timestamp, default = first(timestamp)), units = "hours")),
    
    # If the gap is greater than 6 hours, flag it as a new discrete event
    is_new_event = ifelse(time_gap > 6, 1, 0),
    
    # Cumulative sum generates a unique ID for each continuous temporal block
    sub_event_id = cumsum(is_new_event) + 1
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # Create a global unique Event ID combining physics and time
  mutate(event_id = paste0("Sig", cluster, "_Evt", sub_event_id))

# 2. Aggregate the individual timestamps into discrete Event Profiles
event_summary <- temporal_events %>%
  group_by(cluster, event_id) %>%
  summarize(
    onset_time = min(timestamp),
    resolution_time = max(timestamp),
    # Calculate how long the machine remained in a state of failure
    duration_hrs = as.numeric(difftime(resolution_time, onset_time, units = "hours")),
    peak_severity = max(anomaly_score),
    affected_intervals = n(),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(peak_severity))

# 3. Output the compression results
cat(sprintf("Compressed %d individual anomalies into %d discrete physical events.\n\n", 
            nrow(expanded_anomalies), nrow(event_summary)))

# Display the top 10 most severe discrete events
knitr::kable(head(event_summary, 15))
```

Fault Signatures & Dispatch Routing
Signature 1: The 'Cold Blow' (Mechanical/Thermodynamic)

Symptom: The system draws heavy energy and attempts to heat/cool, but no thermal exchange occurs (e.g., supply temperature flatlines).

Required Personnel: Mechanical HVAC Technician (to inspect stuck actuators, broken boiler valves, or blocked ducts).

Signature 2: The 'Sudden Trip' (Electrical/Kinematic)

Symptom: An instantaneous drop in energy consumption to zero despite a high setpoint demand, resulting in stagnant supply air.

Required Personnel: Licensed Electrician or Building Engineer (to reset tripped breakers, inspect motor relays, or diagnose power loss).

Signature 3: The 'Telemetry Illusion' / 'Envelope Breach' (Digital/Structural)

Symptom: Physically impossible thermodynamics (e.g., room temperature jumping 5°C in 15 minutes with zero energy draw) or a total loss of the thermal boundary.

Required Personnel: IT/Controls Technician (to recalibrate or replace short-circuited sensors) or Facility Management (to secure open doors/windows).


```{r}
#| label: dtw-quantitative-proof
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: true

# install.packages("dtw") # Run in console if needed
library(dtw)
library(purrr)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(cluster)

# 1. Isolate the 52 extreme events and their assigned k=3 clusters
extreme_events <- hvac_scored %>%
  filter(anomaly_score > 0.6) %>%
  # Re-run the strict k=3 clustering for just these 52 to ensure alignment
  mutate(cluster = as.factor(cutree(as.hclust(diana(scale(
    dplyr::select(., temp_error, delta_t, energy_deriv_15m, delta_t_deriv_15m)
  ))), k = 3))) %>%
  dplyr::select(timestamp, cluster)

# 2. Extract a standardized 4-hour MULTIVARIATE time-series matrix for each event
extract_ts_window_multi <- function(target_time) {
  hvac_scored %>%
    filter(
      timestamp >= (target_time - hours(2)),
      timestamp <= (target_time + hours(2))
    ) %>%
    # Select the exact same physics used in the DIANA clustering
    dplyr::select(temp_error, delta_t, energy_deriv_15m, delta_t_deriv_15m) %>%
    # Z-score normalize the entire matrix so energy and temp are on the same scale
    scale() %>% 
    as.matrix()
}

# Apply multivariate extraction to all 52 events
event_ts_list_multi <- map(extreme_events$timestamp, extract_ts_window_multi)
names(event_ts_list_multi) <- paste0("Event_", 1:nrow(extreme_events))

# 3. Compute the O(N^2) MDTW distance matrix
mdtw_dist_matrix <- matrix(NA, nrow = 52, ncol = 52)

for (i in 1:52) {
  for (j in 1:52) {
    # The dtw() function automatically handles matrix vs matrix comparisons
    mdtw_dist_matrix[i, j] <- dtw(event_ts_list_multi[[i]], 
                                  event_ts_list_multi[[j]], 
                                  distance.only = TRUE)$normalizedDistance
  }
}

# 4. Summarize the Intra-Cluster vs Inter-Cluster distances
dtw_results <- expand_grid(
  Event_A = 1:52,
  Event_B = 1:52
) %>%
  mutate(
    Cluster_A = extreme_events$cluster[Event_A],
    Cluster_B = extreme_events$cluster[Event_B],
    Distance = as.vector(mdtw_dist_matrix) # FIXED: Now calling the MDTW matrix
  ) %>%
  filter(Event_A != Event_B) %>% # Remove self-comparisons (distance = 0)
  mutate(Comparison_Type = ifelse(Cluster_A == Cluster_B, 
                                  "Intra-Cluster (Same Fault)", 
                                  "Inter-Cluster (Different Faults)"))

# 5. Print the mathematical proof
dtw_summary <- dtw_results %>%
  group_by(Comparison_Type) %>%
  summarize(
    Mean_Warping_Distance = round(mean(Distance), 2),
    Median_Warping_Distance = round(median(Distance), 2)
  )

print(dtw_summary)
```

```{r}
#| label: monte-carlo-dtw-significance
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: true
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

library(ggplot2)

# 1. Define our observed test statistic (Inter - Intra mean from your tibble)
observed_diff <- 1.80 - 1.33

# 2. Extract the actual distance matrix and true cluster labels
# We use the mdtw_dist_matrix generated in the previous chunk
true_labels <- extreme_events$cluster

# 3. Setup the Monte Carlo permutation test
n_permutations <- 1000
null_distribution <- numeric(n_permutations)

# Set seed for reproducible forensics
set.seed(42)

for(i in 1:n_permutations) {
  # Shuffle the cluster assignments randomly
  shuffled_labels <- sample(true_labels)
  
  # Create a logical matrix to identify which pairs are now "Intra-cluster"
  is_intra <- outer(shuffled_labels, shuffled_labels, "==")
  
  # Use the upper triangle to avoid double counting and self-comparisons
  upper_tri <- upper.tri(mdtw_dist_matrix)
  
  # Extract the randomized distances
  sim_intra_dists <- mdtw_dist_matrix[upper_tri & is_intra]
  sim_inter_dists <- mdtw_dist_matrix[upper_tri & !is_intra]
  
  # Calculate the simulated test statistic for this permutation
  null_distribution[i] <- mean(sim_inter_dists, na.rm = TRUE) - mean(sim_intra_dists, na.rm = TRUE)
}

# 4. Calculate the empirical p-value
p_value <- sum(null_distribution >= observed_diff) / n_permutations

# 5. Visualize the proof
mc_results <- data.frame(Simulated_Diff = null_distribution)

ggplot(mc_results, aes(x = Simulated_Diff)) +
  geom_histogram(fill = "gray70", color = "black", bins = 30) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = observed_diff, color = "darkred", linewidth = 1.5, linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Monte Carlo Permutation Test: Cluster Homogeneity",
    subtitle = sprintf("Observed Difference = %s | p-value = %s (Based on %d permutations)", 
                       observed_diff, format.pval(p_value, eps = 0.001), n_permutations),
    x = "Difference (Inter-Cluster Mean - Intra-Cluster Mean)",
    y = "Frequency in Random Assignments"
  ) +
  annotate("text", x = observed_diff, y = Inf, label = "Our Model's Reality", 
           color = "darkred", vjust = 2, hjust = -0.1, fontface = "bold")
```

Here is the exact formula we are coding for the multivariate $T$ statistic between any two clusters $C_k$ and $C_l$:
$$T_{kl} = \frac{m(C_k, C_l)}{s(C_k) + s(C_l)}$$
Where:
- $m(C_k, C_l)$: The average pairwise distance between elements of different clusters.
- $s(C_k)$: The average pairwise distance within a single cluster.

```{r}
#| label: sobolev-t-statistic-matrix
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: true

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# 1. Define the mathematical helper functions for the Sobolev T-statistic
calc_s <- function(dist_mat, indices) {
  # Average intra-cluster distance
  n <- length(indices)
  if (n < 2) return(NA) # Cannot compute for single-element clusters
  sub_mat <- dist_mat[indices, indices]
  # Sum only the upper triangle to avoid double counting, then apply formula
  return(sum(sub_mat[upper.tri(sub_mat)]) * 2 / (n * (n - 1)))
}

calc_m <- function(dist_mat, indices_k, indices_l) {
  # Average inter-cluster distance
  nk <- length(indices_k)
  nl <- length(indices_l)
  if (nk == 0 | nl == 0) return(NA)
  sub_mat <- dist_mat[indices_k, indices_l]
  return(sum(sub_mat) / (nk * nl))
}

calc_T_matrix <- function(dist_mat, labels) {
  # Generate the full pairwise T-statistic matrix for k clusters
  unique_clusters <- sort(unique(labels))
  k <- length(unique_clusters)
  T_mat <- matrix(NA, nrow = k, ncol = k, 
                  dimnames = list(unique_clusters, unique_clusters))
  
  # Precompute s(C) for all clusters to save redundant operations
  s_vals <- sapply(unique_clusters, function(c) {
    calc_s(dist_mat, which(labels == c))
  })
  
  # Calculate T_kl for the upper triangle
  for (i in 1:(k-1)) {
    for (j in (i+1):k) {
      idx_k <- which(labels == unique_clusters[i])
      idx_l <- which(labels == unique_clusters[j])
      
      m_val <- calc_m(dist_mat, idx_k, idx_l)
      T_mat[i, j] <- m_val / (s_vals[i] + s_vals[j])
    }
  }
  return(T_mat)
}

# 2. Calculate the True Observed T-Matrix
true_labels <- extreme_events$cluster
observed_T_mat <- calc_T_matrix(mdtw_dist_matrix, true_labels)

# 3. Execute the Size-Preserved Monte Carlo Permutations
n_permutations <- 1000
set.seed(42)

# Initialize an array to hold all 1000 simulated 3x3 matrices
sim_T_arrays <- array(NA, dim = c(3, 3, n_permutations))

for (p in 1:n_permutations) {
  # Shuffling the labels vector guarantees identical group sizes |Ck| and |Cl|
  shuffled_labels <- sample(true_labels)
  sim_T_arrays[, , p] <- calc_T_matrix(mdtw_dist_matrix, shuffled_labels)
}

# 4. Calculate the empirical p-value element-by-element
p_value_mat <- matrix(NA, nrow = 3, ncol = 3, 
                      dimnames = dimnames(observed_T_mat))

for (i in 1:2) {
  for (j in (i+1):3) {
    obs_val <- observed_T_mat[i, j]
    # Extract the vector of 1000 simulated values for this specific T_kl pair
    sim_vals <- sim_T_arrays[i, j, ]
    
    # Calculate how often a random distribution generated a T-stat >= our observed
    p_value_mat[i, j] <- sum(sim_vals >= obs_val, na.rm = TRUE) / n_permutations
  }
}

# 5. Format and print the final proof
results_df <- data.frame(
  Pair = c("Sig 1 vs Sig 2", "Sig 1 vs Sig 3", "Sig 2 vs Sig 3"),
  Observed_T = c(observed_T_mat[1,2], observed_T_mat[1,3], observed_T_mat[2,3]),
  p_value = c(p_value_mat[1,2], p_value_mat[1,3], p_value_mat[2,3])
) %>%
  mutate(
    Observed_T = round(Observed_T, 3),
    Significance = ifelse(p_value < 0.001, "< 0.001", as.character(p_value))
  )

cat("--- Sobolev Multivariate T-Statistic Matrix Proof ---\n\n")
print(results_df, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: sobolev-k4-stress-test
#| warning: false

# 1. Force DIANA to split the data into 4 clusters instead of 3
extreme_events_k4 <- hvac_scored %>%
  filter(anomaly_score > 0.6) %>%
  mutate(cluster = as.factor(cutree(as.hclust(diana(scale(
    dplyr::select(., temp_error, delta_t, energy_deriv_15m, delta_t_deriv_15m)
  ))), k = 4)))

true_labels_k4 <- extreme_events_k4$cluster

# 2. Calculate the True Observed T-Matrix for the 4 clusters
observed_T_mat_k4 <- calc_T_matrix(mdtw_dist_matrix, true_labels_k4)

# 3. Execute the Size-Preserved Monte Carlo Permutations
n_permutations <- 10000
set.seed(42)

sim_T_arrays_k4 <- array(NA, dim = c(4, 4, n_permutations))

for (p in 1:n_permutations) {
  shuffled_labels_k4 <- sample(true_labels_k4)
  sim_T_arrays_k4[, , p] <- calc_T_matrix(mdtw_dist_matrix, shuffled_labels_k4)
}

# 4. Calculate the empirical p-value for all 6 possible pairs
pairs_list <- list()
row_idx <- 1

for (i in 1:3) {
  for (j in (i+1):4) {
    obs_val <- observed_T_mat_k4[i, j]
    sim_vals <- sim_T_arrays_k4[i, j, ]
    p_val <- sum(sim_vals >= obs_val, na.rm = TRUE) / n_permutations
    
    pairs_list[[row_idx]] <- data.frame(
      Pair = paste("Sig", i, "vs Sig", j),
      Observed_T = obs_val,
      p_value = p_val
    )
    row_idx <- row_idx + 1
  }
}

# 5. Format and print the final proof
results_k4 <- bind_rows(pairs_list) %>%
  mutate(
    Observed_T = round(Observed_T, 4),
    Significance = ifelse(p_value < 0.0001, "< 0.0001", as.character(signif(p_value, 3)))
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(p_value), Observed_T) # Sort so the worst pair bubbles to the top

cat("--- Sobolev T-Statistic Proof (Forced k=4 Split) ---\n\n")
print(results_k4, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: extract-cluster-archetypes

# 1. Add original row indices to keep track of the matrix positions
extreme_events <- extreme_events %>%
  mutate(matrix_idx = row_number())

# 2. Function to find the Medoid for a given cluster
get_cluster_medoid <- function(target_cluster) {
  # Get the matrix indices for the events in this cluster
  cluster_indices <- extreme_events %>%
    filter(cluster == target_cluster) %>%
    pull(matrix_idx)
  
  # Subset the MDTW distance matrix for just these events
  sub_matrix <- mdtw_dist_matrix[cluster_indices, cluster_indices]
  
  # Find the local index with the minimum sum of distances to all others
  medoid_local_idx <- which.min(rowSums(sub_matrix))
  
  # Map back to the global event ID and timestamp
  medoid_global_idx <- cluster_indices[medoid_local_idx]
  medoid_timestamp <- extreme_events$timestamp[medoid_global_idx]
  
  return(medoid_timestamp)
}

# 3. Extract the exact timestamps for the three Archetypes
archetype_sig1 <- get_cluster_medoid(1)
archetype_sig2 <- get_cluster_medoid(2)
archetype_sig3 <- get_cluster_medoid(3)

cat(sprintf("Archetype for Signature 1 (Cold Blow): %s\n", archetype_sig1))
cat(sprintf("Archetype for Signature 2 (Sudden Trip): %s\n", archetype_sig2))
cat(sprintf("Archetype for Signature 3 (Envelope/Digital): %s\n\n", archetype_sig3))

# 4. Visualize the Archetypes individually
plot_a1 <- plot_blast_radius(archetype_sig1, "ARCHETYPE: Signature 1 (The Cold Blow)")
plot_a2 <- plot_blast_radius(archetype_sig2, "ARCHETYPE: Signature 2 (The Sudden Trip)")
plot_a3 <- plot_blast_radius(archetype_sig3, "ARCHETYPE: Signature 3 (The Envelope Breach)")

# Print sequentially instead of wrapping into a single mega-plot
plot_a1
plot_a2
plot_a3
```

```{r}
#| label: optimize-k-non-monotonic
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: true
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

library(cluster)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Re-establish the baseline DIANA clustering tree
event_features <- hvac_scored %>%
  filter(anomaly_score > 0.6) %>%
  dplyr::select(temp_error, delta_t, energy_deriv_15m, delta_t_deriv_15m) %>%
  scale()

# Compute the hierarchical tree once
hc_tree <- as.hclust(diana(event_features))

# 2. Define the Harmonic Pairwise Silhouette function
calc_harmonic_pairwise_sil <- function(dist_mat, labels) {
  k_unique <- sort(unique(labels))
  k <- length(k_unique)
  
  pairwise_means <- c()
  
  for (i in 1:(k-1)) {
    for (j in (i+1):k) {
      cl_A <- k_unique[i]
      cl_B <- k_unique[j]
      
      idx <- which(labels %in% c(cl_A, cl_B))
      sub_mat <- dist_mat[idx, idx]
      sub_labels <- as.character(labels[idx])
      
      # Calculate silhouette for this specific pair
      sil_obj <- silhouette(as.numeric(as.factor(sub_labels)), dmatrix = sub_mat)
      mean_sil <- mean(sil_obj[, "sil_width"])
      
      # Strict Penalty: Clamp negative/zero scores to 0.001 to penalize the harmonic mean
      if (is.na(mean_sil) || mean_sil <= 0) mean_sil <- 0.001 
      
      pairwise_means <- c(pairwise_means, mean_sil)
    }
  }
  
  # Harmonic Mean formula: m / sum(1/x)
  h_mean <- length(pairwise_means) / sum(1 / pairwise_means)
  return(h_mean)
}

# 3. Define the Global Silhouette function
calc_global_sil <- function(dist_mat, labels) {
  sil_obj <- silhouette(as.numeric(as.factor(labels)), dmatrix = dist_mat)
  return(mean(sil_obj[, "sil_width"]))
}

# 4. Execute the iteration loop
k_values <- 2:6
results <- data.frame(
  k = k_values, 
  Global_Silhouette = NA, 
  Harmonic_Pairwise = NA
)

for (i in seq_along(k_values)) {
  current_k <- k_values[i]
  current_labels <- cutree(hc_tree, k = current_k)
  
  results$Global_Silhouette[i] <- calc_global_sil(mdtw_dist_matrix, current_labels)
  results$Harmonic_Pairwise[i] <- calc_harmonic_pairwise_sil(mdtw_dist_matrix, current_labels)
}

# 5. Print the numerical results
cat("--- Cluster Integrity Analysis (k = 2 to 6) ---\n\n")
print(results %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 3))))

# 6. Plot the Non-Monotonic Curves
results_long <- results %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Global_Silhouette, Harmonic_Pairwise), 
               names_to = "Metric", values_to = "Score") %>%
  mutate(Metric = ifelse(Metric == "Global_Silhouette", 
                         "Global Silhouette (Standard)", 
                         "Harmonic Pairwise (Strict Penalty)"))

ggplot(results_long, aes(x = k, y = Score, color = Metric)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Global Silhouette (Standard)" = "steelblue", 
                                "Harmonic Pairwise (Strict Penalty)" = "darkred")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Self-Tuning k-Optimization: Finding the Fracture Point",
    subtitle = "Tracking geometric integrity of MDTW distances across cluster counts",
    x = "Number of Clusters (k)",
    y = "Effect Size / Integrity Score"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.title = element_blank())
```

```{r}
#| label: optimize-k-weighted-harmonic
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: true
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

# 1. Define the Weighted Harmonic Pairwise Silhouette function
calc_weighted_harmonic_sil <- function(dist_mat, labels) {
  k_unique <- sort(unique(labels))
  k <- length(k_unique)
  
  pairwise_scores <- c()
  pairwise_weights <- c()
  
  for (i in 1:(k-1)) {
    for (j in (i+1):k) {
      cl_A <- k_unique[i]
      cl_B <- k_unique[j]
      
      idx <- which(labels %in% c(cl_A, cl_B))
      sub_mat <- dist_mat[idx, idx]
      sub_labels <- as.character(labels[idx])
      
      # Calculate silhouette
      sil_obj <- silhouette(as.numeric(as.factor(sub_labels)), dmatrix = sub_mat)
      mean_sil <- mean(sil_obj[, "sil_width"])
      
      if (is.na(mean_sil) || mean_sil <= 0) mean_sil <- 0.001 
      
      pairwise_scores <- c(pairwise_scores, mean_sil)
      
      # The Fix: Weight by the combined operational volume of the two clusters
      weight <- sum(labels == cl_A) + sum(labels == cl_B)
      pairwise_weights <- c(pairwise_weights, weight)
    }
  }
  
  # Weighted Harmonic Mean formula
  w_h_mean <- sum(pairwise_weights) / sum(pairwise_weights / pairwise_scores)
  return(w_h_mean)
}

# 2. Execute the iteration loop
results_weighted <- data.frame(
  k = k_values, 
  Global_Silhouette = results$Global_Silhouette, # Re-use from previous chunk
  Weighted_Harmonic = NA
)

for (i in seq_along(k_values)) {
  current_labels <- cutree(hc_tree, k = k_values[i])
  results_weighted$Weighted_Harmonic[i] <- calc_weighted_harmonic_sil(mdtw_dist_matrix, current_labels)
}

# 3. Plot the Corrected Curves
results_w_long <- results_weighted %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Global_Silhouette, Weighted_Harmonic), 
               names_to = "Metric", values_to = "Score") %>%
  mutate(Metric = ifelse(Metric == "Global_Silhouette", 
                         "Global Silhouette (Standard)", 
                         "Weighted Harmonic (Size-Penalized)"))

ggplot(results_w_long, aes(x = k, y = Score, color = Metric)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Global Silhouette (Standard)" = "steelblue", 
                                "Weighted Harmonic (Size-Penalized)" = "darkorange3")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Self-Tuning k-Optimization: The Size-Weighted Correction",
    subtitle = "Accounting for operational volume to eliminate micro-cluster bias",
    x = "Number of Clusters (k)",
    y = "Effect Size / Integrity Score"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.title = element_blank())
```

```{r}
#| label: optimize-k-product-weighted
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: true
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

calc_product_weighted_harmonic_sil <- function(dist_mat, labels) {
  k_unique <- sort(unique(labels))
  k <- length(k_unique)
  
  pairwise_scores <- c()
  pairwise_weights <- c()
  
  for (i in 1:(k-1)) {
    for (j in (i+1):k) {
      cl_A <- k_unique[i]
      cl_B <- k_unique[j]
      
      idx <- which(labels %in% c(cl_A, cl_B))
      sub_mat <- dist_mat[idx, idx]
      sub_labels <- as.character(labels[idx])
      
      sil_obj <- silhouette(as.numeric(as.factor(sub_labels)), dmatrix = sub_mat)
      mean_sil <- mean(sil_obj[, "sil_width"])
      
      if (is.na(mean_sil) || mean_sil <= 0) mean_sil <- 0.001 
      
      pairwise_scores <- c(pairwise_scores, mean_sil)
      
      # The Edge-Weight Fix: Product instead of Sum
      weight <- sum(labels == cl_A) * sum(labels == cl_B)
      # weight <- sqrt((1/sum(labels == cl_A))) + sqrt((1/sum(labels == cl_B)))
      pairwise_weights <- c(pairwise_weights, weight)
    }
  }
  
  # Weighted Harmonic Mean formula remains structurally the same
  w_h_mean <- sum(pairwise_weights) / sum(pairwise_weights / pairwise_scores)
  return(w_h_mean)
}

# Execute the iteration loop for the new metric
results_prod_weighted <- data.frame(k = 2:6, Product_Weighted_Harmonic = NA)

for (i in seq_along(results_prod_weighted$k)) {
  current_labels <- cutree(hc_tree, k = results_prod_weighted$k[i])
  results_prod_weighted$Product_Weighted_Harmonic[i] <- calc_product_weighted_harmonic_sil(
    mdtw_dist_matrix, current_labels
  )
}

# Print the numerical results to see if the peak shifted
print(results_prod_weighted %>% mutate(Product_Weighted_Harmonic = round(Product_Weighted_Harmonic, 3)))
```

Optimal weight is product cluster sizes.
